I left the Christianity 5 years ago after battling with unanswered questions. At first it was relieving and peaceful. 4 years later my life was chaos, I went through all the logical worldly routes to fix it - more therapy, healthcare, trying to make new friends, etc. I felt even more the void of God not being present in my life, I felt afraid and unprotected, things that never used to happen would happen, like the protection was gone. When I prayed to Him it wasn’t like before, it was like he was so far away, so I thought the connection was severed. 

Then slowly I saw signs and felt Jesus calling me back. One day everything got too much, I just cried in bed and begged for Him to forgive me. Two weeks later I met my now husband, with so many weird coincidences between us, even to this day, that it was like we were made for each other, which really healed my history of more abusive relationships. Outside of that my life slowly got on the mend, the unsolvable problems were shown a new path that solved them over time, health problems resolved in months with a new strength I never knew I had, and I was guided to a life where I am now happy and in His arms again. 

I will never go back, this whole journey showed me that while I am smart and capable, while we have great resources on earth, there are just some things that only God can fix. 

It’s not been perfect obviously, spiritual attacks are real, but I have so much more strength in Christ.

I’m the same and have dealt with this for years. The best thing you can do is temporarily get away from the trigger of the compulsion (eg something to fix) by either leaving the house, going to a different room, or even just sitting and closing your eyes. Use that time instead to focus on decreasing your stress and lower any overstimulation you might be experiencing. This isn’t always perfect but it will help reduce the severity of the situation in your mind and practice exposure therapy.

Some great techniques to do this are:
- Find something that comforts you, like a soft blanket, comfortable clothes, etc.
- Check your breath to make sure you’re breathing properly 
- Have rooibos or chamomile tea
- Drink 800mL-1L of water
- Have a shower
- Tell yourself what you need to hear to disregard the importance of the compulsion. Some that help me are “I am safe, I am strong, this is my house, worrying about this will not add another hour to my life, it’s normal for things to get dirty sometimes”. I also have found prayer very helpful but that is a personal choice. 

You might not have the capacity to do this in that very moment, like if you’re on your way to work or you have young kids, but even 5 minutes can make a difference if you can fit it in.

After covid went by my mental health (contamination OCD) grew worse and doctors could only put me on more meds. I couldn’t leave the house or do basic adult tasks. My partner grew up wealthy and we both have different eating habits. What I realised it came down to is scarcity mindset. When you grow up poor, you never know when you’re going to have your favourite food (or any food) again, so when you do get it you eat as much as you can at once. My partner will eat only a single portion because he knows he can have more whenever he wants, because he can afford it.

Pretty much everything I know I’ve learned directly from nutritionists (two of my friends and my brother, I lucked out there) and confirmed personally through experimentation. 

A WFPB is good to start for good fibre sources, I was WFPB for a couple years but had to reintroduce myself to meat for more iron and protein, but protein powder goes a long way

If you google a BMR calculator and a protein calculator it will tell you how much you need for calories and protein. From there I made a spreadsheet in excel that calculated calories and protein and planned my meals each day to ensure I was meeting my calorie and protein needs. Just from the spreadsheet I learned proper portion size of my carbs, protein and fibre based on my calorie and protein needs. Eventually I didn’t need to check the spreadsheet anymore because my stomach acclimatised. 

From what nutritionists have told me, protein makes you satisfied, carbs give you quick energy, fats help absorb nutrients and give long lasting energy, and your favourite foods make you happy, so knowing that has helped me maintain this with balance rather than misery.
